name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
department: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / NABARD, via participating banks
summary: Low-interest credit line for farmers to cover cultivation costs, post-harvest expenses, and allied agricultural activities, at an effective interest rate of around 4% with prompt repayment.
eligibility: Individual or joint owner-cultivators of agricultural land
Tenant farmers, oral lessees, and sharecroppers
Self Help Groups (SHGs) and Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) of farmers
Age 18-75 years (co-borrower required for applicants above 60)
documents: Identity proof (Aadhaar, voter ID, driving licence, or passport)
Proof of land holding certified by revenue authorities
Details of crops cultivated and land area
fee: No application fee. Effective interest rate is about 4% per annum on loans up to ₹5 lakh, after a 2% interest subvention plus a 3% Prompt Repayment Incentive from the government.
process: Apply via the Jan Samarth portal, or directly at any participating bank branch
Provide land records, cropping pattern, and identity/address documents
Bank assesses credit limit using the Scale of Finance formula (crop type × land area, plus allowances)
KCC is sanctioned and linked to a RuPay Kisan Credit Card for cash withdrawal at ATMs/PoS
Renew annually based on updated land records and repayment history
source: NABARD / Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare

faq.question: What is the maximum KCC credit limit?
faq.answer: Up to ₹5 lakh benefits from the government interest subvention (raised from ₹3 lakh in Budget 2025-26). Higher limits are possible but lose the subsidised interest rate on the excess amount.

faq.question: Can tenant farmers apply for KCC?
faq.answer: Yes — tenant farmers, oral lessees, sharecroppers, and members of Self Help Groups/Joint Liability Groups are all eligible, not just landowners.
